fullPassage: Hughie is a charming young man who has achieved everything except making money. He is in love with Laura Merton, the daughter of a retired colonel. Laura loves him sincerely, but the Colonel won't let them marry until Hughie has 10,000 pounds. One day, Hughie dropped by to see his friend Alan Trevor, a painter. He was adding the finishing touches to a painting of a beggar. In the studio, the beggar himself was standing on a raised platform. He was an old man with a very pitiful face. His clothes were old and worn out. "Poor old man!" said Hughie. "How unfortunate he looks! But I suppose, for you painters, his face is his fortune?" "Certainly," replied Alan, "you wouldn't want a beggar to look happy, would you?" "How much does a model get for sitting?" asked Hughie. "A shilling an hour," answered Alan. "And how much do you get for your picture, Alan?" asked Hughie. "Oh, for this I get two thousand!" "Pounds?" "Guineas. Painters, poets, and doctors always get guineas." "Well, I think the model should get a fair share of that," cried Hughie, laughing. He continued, "as they work just as hard as you do." "Nonsense, nonsense! Look at the effort it takes to draw and paint and stand in front of the canvas all day! You mustn't talk. I'm very busy. Keep quiet," said Alan. After a while, the servant came in and told Alan that the frame-maker wanted to see him. Alan said, "I will be back in a moment," as he went out. The old beggar took advantage of Alan's absence to rest for a moment on a chair. He looked so sad and lonely. Hughie couldn't help pitying him and felt his own pockets to see what money he had. All he could find, however, was a few coins. "Poor old fellow, he wants them more than I do, but it means no carriage for two weeks," he thought to himself. He walked across the studio and put the coins into the beggar's hand. The old man was surprised and smiled faintly. "Thank you, sir," he said. Then Alan arrived, and Hughie said goodbye, blushing a little at what he had done. Hughie spent the day with Laura, received a gentle scolding for his actions, and had to walk home. That night he walked into the Palette Club at about eleven o'clock and found Alan sitting alone. Hughie asked, "Hey, Alan! Have you got that picture finished?" and Alan replied, "Finished and framed!" Then, Alan continued, "And by the way, that old model you saw is quite devoted to you. He wanted to know who you are, where you live, and what your prospects are." "My dear Alan," cried Hughie, "I shall probably find him waiting for me when I go home. Poor old man! I wish I could do something for him. I have some old clothes at home — do you think he would like any of them? His clothes were worn, falling to pieces." "But he looks wonderful in them," said Alan. "What you call worn clothes I call romance. I find them romantic and appealing. However, I'll tell him about your offer." When Hughie commented seriously, "You painters are heartless," Alan replied, "An artist's heart is his head. Our job is to show the world as we see it, not to reform it as we know it. Now tell me how Laura is. The old model was quite interested in her." "You don't mean to say you talked to him about her?" said Hughie. "Sure I did. He knows all about the Colonel, Laura, and the 10,000 pounds," replied Alan. "You told that old beggar all my private affairs?" cried Hughie, looking very red and angry. "My dear boy," said Alan, smiling, "that old beggar, as you call him, is one of the richest men in Europe. He is Baron Hausberg. He is a great friend of mine, buys all my pictures, and asked me a month ago to paint him as a beggar." "Baron Hausberg!" cried Hughie, feeling embarrassed. "Good heavens! I gave him some coins," he said, sinking into an armchair. "What? You gave him coins?" cried Alan, bursting into laughter. He went on, "Well, it never occurred to me that you would distribute money in that way. Besides, when you came in, I didn't know if Hausberg would like his name mentioned. You know he wasn't in full dress." "Oh no, what did I do? The best thing I can do is to go to bed, and, my dear Alan, you mustn't tell anyone," said Hughie, and he went home, feeling very unhappy. The next morning, when Hughie was having breakfast, an old gentleman visited his house. The man said, "I have come from Baron Hausberg," and continued, "The Baron ...." Hughie interrupted, "I beg, sir, that you will offer him my sincerest apologies." Then, with a smile, the old gentleman said, "The Baron has asked me to bring you this letter," and gave Hughie a sealed envelope. On the outside was written, "A wedding present to Hughie Erskine and Laura Merton, from an old beggar," and inside was a check for 10,000 pounds. When they were married, Alan was the best man, and the Baron made a speech at the wedding. "Millionaire models," remarked Alan, "are rare enough, but model millionaires are rarer still!"

화가는 청년이 그런 식으로 돈을 나눠 줄 것을 미리 알고 있었다.
남작은 정장을 갖춰 입은 채로 모델을 섰다.

questions.passage: Hughie is a charming young man who has achieved everything except making money. He is in love with Laura Merton, the daughter of a retired colonel. Laura loves him sincerely, but the Colonel won't let them marry until Hughie has 10,000 pounds. One day, Hughie dropped by to see his friend Alan Trevor, a painter. He was adding the finishing touches to a painting of a beggar. In the studio, the beggar himself was standing on a raised platform. He was an old man with a very pitiful face. His clothes were old and worn out.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④ 누추한 거지가 사실 부유한 남작이었다는 숨겨진 정체
det.analysis:
❌ ① the technical steps a painter follows to finish a portrait(화가가 초상화를 완성하는 기술적 단계): 그림 기법은 배경일 뿐 주제가 아니에요.

❌ ② the daily duties of a servant in a wealthy household(부유한 집안 하인의 일상 업무): 하인은 잠깐 등장할 뿐이에요.

❌ ③ the history of quiz shows in nineteenth-century Europe(19세기 유럽 퀴즈 쇼의 역사): 본문에 없는 내용이에요.

✅ ④ the hidden identity of a ragged beggar who was really a wealthy baron(누추한 거지가 사실 부유한 남작이었다는 숨겨진 정체): 겉모습만 보고 거지라 여긴 모델이 사실 유럽 최고 부자인 남작이었다는 이야기 전체를 아울러요 ←정답
det.tip: 거지로 보였던 모델의 진짜 정체가 글의 핵심입니다.

questions.passage: Hughie is a charming young man who has achieved everything except making money. He is in love with Laura Merton, the daughter of a retired colonel. Laura loves him sincerely, but the Colonel won't let them marry until Hughie has 10,000 pounds. One day, Hughie dropped by to see his friend Alan Trevor, a painter. He was adding the finishing touches to a painting of a beggar. In the studio, the beggar himself was standing on a raised platform. He was an old man with a very pitiful face. His clothes were old and worn out.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① 보상받은 선한 마음: 남작이었던 거지
det.analysis:
이야기는 청년이 불쌍히 여겨 동전을 준 '거지'가 사실 남작이었고, 그 선행이 뜻밖의 결혼 선물로 돌아오는 내용이에요.

✅ ① A Kind Heart Rewarded: The Beggar Who Was a Baron(보상받은 선한 마음: 남작이었던 거지): 선행이 보상으로 돌아온 반전을 압축한 제목이에요 ←정답

❌ ② The Painter Who Refused to Sell His Pictures(그림 팔기를 거부한 화가): 화가는 오히려 남작에게 그림을 다 팔아요.

❌ ③ How to Become a Famous Portrait Painter(유명 초상화가가 되는 법): 실용 안내가 아니에요.

❌ ④ The Dangers of Lending Money to Close Friends(친한 친구에게 돈을 빌려주는 위험): 돈을 빌려준 이야기가 아니에요.
det.tip: 선한 마음 → 뜻밖의 보상, 거지의 정체 = 남작이 제목의 핵심입니다.

questions.passage: "What you call worn clothes I call romance. I find them romantic and appealing. However, I'll tell him about your offer." When Hughie commented seriously, "You painters are heartless," Alan replied, "<u>An artist's heart is his head</u>. Our job is to show the world as we see it, not to reform it as we know it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 An artist's heart is his head가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② 예술가는 감정이 아니라 이성(머리)으로 세상을 보고 표현한다
det.analysis:
밑줄 'An artist's heart is his head(예술가의 심장은 그의 머리에 있다)'는, 바로 뒤 'Our job is to show the world as we see it, not to reform it(세상을 보는 그대로 보여 주는 것이 우리 일이다)'과 이어져요. 즉 예술가는 감정이 아니라 이성(머리)으로 세상을 관찰·표현한다는 뜻이에요.

❌ ① 감정을 최우선으로 삼는다는 것은 'heart is his head'와 반대예요.

✅ ② 예술가는 감정보다 이성(머리)으로 세상을 본다는 의미예요 ←정답

❌ ③ 돈에 관한 내용이 아니에요.

❌ ④ 타인의 마음을 읽는다는 내용이 아니에요.
det.tip: heart is his head = 예술가는 감정이 아니라 이성(머리)으로 세상을 본다

questions.passage: Hughie is a charming young man who has achieved everything except making money. <u>He</u> is in love with Laura Merton, the daughter of a retired colonel. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 He가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ 돈 버는 것을 빼고 거의 모든 것을 이룬 젊은이(Hughie)
det.analysis:
밑줄 문장: 'He is in love with Laura Merton, the daughter of a retired colonel.'(그는 은퇴한 대령의 딸인 Laura Merton을 사랑하고 있다). 바로 앞 문장 'Hughie is a charming young man who has achieved everything except making money'에서 소개한 Hughie를 He가 받아요.

❌ ① 은퇴한 대령은 Laura의 아버지로 He가 아니에요.

❌ ② 화가는 뒤에 등장하는 인물이에요.

✅ ③ 돈 버는 것을 빼고 모든 것을 이룬 젊은이(Hughie)가 He가 가리키는 대상이에요 ←정답

❌ ④ Laura가 사랑하는 남자는 바로 Hughie 자신이에요.
det.tip: 앞 문장의 주인공 청년(Hughie) → 다음 문장의 He로 이어집니다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 falling to pieces(너덜너덜 해진)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① neatly pressed(깔끔하게 다려진): 앞의 'worn(해진)'과 모순
❌ ② made of silk(비단으로 만든): 거지의 낡은 옷과 어울리지 않음
✅ ③ falling to pieces(너덜너덜 해진): 거지의 옷이 'worn(해지고)' 조각조각 '떨어져 나갈' 지경이라는 문맥에 적절. Hughie가 낡은 옷을 주고 싶어 하는 이유가 됨 ← 정답
❌ ④ kept in a box(상자에 보관된): 입고 있는 낡은 옷의 상태와 무관
det.tip: His clothes were worn, falling to pieces: 해지고 너덜너덜한 옷

"그는 나의 절친한 친구이다." (7단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) He, a, friend, great, is, mine, of 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: He is a great friend of mine
det.analysis:
주어는 He, be동사는 현재시제 is예요: He + is.

'절친한 친구'는 a great friend로 써요: a + great + friend.

'나의'는 소유를 나타내는 of mine으로 뒤에 붙여요: of + mine.

순서대로 이으면 He / is / a / great / friend / of / mine.

questions.passage: He walked across the studio and put the coins into the beggar's hand. The old man was __________ (surprise) and smiled faintly. "Thank you, sir," he said. Then Alan arrived, and Hughie said goodbye, blushing a little at what he had done.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 흐름에 맞도록 괄호 안에 주어진 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: surprised (감정을 느끼는 주체 → 과거분사형).
det.analysis: 구문 분석: 'The old man was ___ and smiled faintly'에서 빈칸은 be동사 was의 보어 자리예요. 사람(노인)이 감정을 '느끼는' 주체일 때는 과거분사형 형용사를 써요. 따라서 surprise를 surprised로 바꿔 'was surprised(놀랐다)'로 써야 해요. 사물·원인이 '놀라게 하는' 경우에만 surprising을 써요.
det.tip: 사람이 감정을 느낌 → 과거분사 surprised(be surprised=놀라다)

"그 늙은 모델은 그녀에게 아주 관심이 많았다." (8단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) The, her, in, interested, model, old, quite, was 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 8단어로 쓸 것 (be interested in 구문 활용)

det.korean: The old model was quite interested in her
det.analysis:
주어는 '그 늙은 모델'이에요: The + old + model.

be동사 과거형 was 뒤에 '~에 관심이 있는'은 과거분사형 interested를 써요. '아주'는 부사 quite로 강조해요: was + quite + interested.

'그녀에게'는 전치사 in을 써서 be interested in의 형태로 이어요: in + her.

순서대로 이으면 The / old / model / was / quite / interested / in / her.
det.tip: be interested in ~(~에 관심이 있다) + 강조 부사 quite

[ a / beggar / himself / on / platform / raised / standing / the / was ] (9단어) (영어로)

det.korean: the beggar himself was standing on a raised platform
det.analysis:
주어는 '그 거지 자신'으로, 강조의 재귀대명사 himself를 붙여요: the + beggar + himself.

'서 있었다'는 과거진행형 was standing으로 써요: was + standing.

'높인 단상 위에'는 on a raised platform으로 이어요(raised는 '높인'이라는 과거분사형 형용사): on + a + raised + platform.

순서대로 이으면 the / beggar / himself / was / standing / on / a / raised / platform.
det.tip: 재귀대명사 강조(himself) + 과거진행(was standing) + on a raised platform

"그 모델도 그것의 공정한 몫을 받아야 한다." (9단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) a, fair, get, model, of, share, should, that, the 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 9단어로 쓸 것 (조동사 should + 동사원형 활용)

det.korean: the model should get a fair share of that
det.analysis:
주어는 '그 모델'이에요: the + model.

'받아야 한다'는 조동사 should 뒤에 동사원형 get을 써요: should + get.

'공정한 몫'은 a fair share, '그것의'는 of that으로 이어요: a + fair + share + of + that.

순서대로 이으면 the / model / should / get / a / fair / share / of / that.
det.tip: 조동사 should + 동사원형(get), a fair share of that(그것의 공정한 몫)
